Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.25. Source: Kubernetes Deprecated API Migration Guide (official_deprecation_notice). Section: Removed APIs by release / v1.25 / EndpointSlice.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Migrate manifests and API clients to use the discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.21.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Removed APIs by release / v1.25 / EndpointSlice: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25. Migrate manifests and API clients to use the discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.21. All existing persisted objects are accessible via the new API Notable changes in discovery.k8s.io/v1: * use per Endpoint nodeName field instead of deprecated topology["kubernetes.io/hostname"] field * use per Endpoint zone field instead of deprecated topology["topology.kubernetes.io/zone"] field * topology is replaced with the deprecatedTopology field which is not writable in v1
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.25 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25. Manifests and API clients still using v1beta1 will break after upgrading past 1.25 and must be migrated to discovery.k8s.io/v1, available since v1.21.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.25, where discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice stops being served.
quotes: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25.
conditions.relevance: Establishes that the removal occurs in 1.25, which is between 1.23 and 1.29.

conditions.statement: Manifests or API clients use the discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice.
quotes: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.21.
conditions.relevance: Only manifests and clients that use the v1beta1 EndpointSlice API are affected by the removal.

conditions.statement: Manifests and clients already use discovery.k8s.io/v1, so the risk does not apply.
quotes: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.21.
conditions.relevance: If all usage is already on v1 (available since v1.21), the removal of v1beta1 has no effect.

suggested_actions: Migrate manifests and API clients to use the discovery.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.21.
Existing persisted objects are accessible via the new API, so no data migration of stored objects is stated as required.

paths.description: In discovery.k8s.io/v1, the per-Endpoint topology map is replaced by the non-writable deprecatedTopology field. Code that reads or writes topology["kubernetes.io/hostname"] or topology["topology.kubernetes.io/zone"] must use the per-Endpoint nodeName and zone fields instead.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.25, where discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 EndpointSlice stops being served and clients must move to v1.
quotes: The discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1 API version of EndpointSlice is no longer served as of v1.25.
conditions.relevance: Clients move to v1 because of this removal, which exposes them to the v1 field changes.

conditions.statement: Application code or manifests use the EndpointSlice topology field with the hostname or zone keys.
quotes: use per Endpoint nodeName field instead of deprecated topology["kubernetes.io/hostname"] field
use per Endpoint zone field instead of deprecated topology["topology.kubernetes.io/zone"] field
conditions.relevance: These topology keys are replaced in v1 by nodeName and zone.
ambiguities: The text does not state whether topology is rejected or silently ignored when written via v1.

conditions.statement: Code writes to the topology field of EndpointSlice endpoints, which is not writable in v1.
quotes: topology is replaced with the deprecatedTopology field which is not writable in v1
conditions.relevance: Writers of the topology field cannot write deprecatedTopology in v1.

suggested_actions: Use the per Endpoint nodeName field instead of topology["kubernetes.io/hostname"].
Use the per Endpoint zone field instead of topology["topology.kubernetes.io/zone"].
Stop writing to topology/deprecatedTopology, which is not writable in v1.
